articles.title: Government Plans to Tax Netflix, Starlink and Other Cross-Border Digital Services
articles.summary: The Government is preparing to introduce a tax framework for cross-border digital services such as Netflix, Starlink, and other international online platforms. Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Nyarko Ampem says the move is aimed at ensuring foreign digital service providers contribute fairly to Ghana's tax revenue.

content.html:
The Government has announced plans to introduce a tax regime targeting cross-border digital services, a move that could affect popular platforms such as Netflix, Starlink, and other international subscription-based services used by Ghanaians.


Speaking on the proposal, Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Nyarko Ampem said the increasing use of foreign digital platforms has created the need for a system that ensures these companies contribute their fair share of taxes to Ghana's economy.

According to him, millions of Ghanaians now rely on international digital services for entertainment, internet connectivity, cloud computing, software subscriptions, and other online activities. However, many of these companies generate revenue from Ghana without having a significant physical presence in the country.

The proposed tax framework is expected to align Ghana with a growing global trend, where governments are introducing measures to tax multinational digital companies that earn income from local users. Authorities argue that such policies promote tax fairness by ensuring both local and foreign businesses operate under comparable tax obligations.


While the government believes the initiative could increase domestic revenue and strengthen public finances, the proposal is also likely to spark debate among consumers and businesses. Some observers have expressed concern that digital service providers could pass any additional tax costs on to customers through higher subscription fees.

The announcement comes as Ghana continues to explore new sources of revenue to support public spending and adapt its tax system to the rapidly expanding digital economy. Officials maintain that the objective is not to discourage innovation or digital adoption but to ensure the tax system keeps pace with changing patterns of commerce.

Further details, including which services will be affected, the proposed tax rates, and the timeline for implementation, are expected to be announced as government develops the new framework.

articles.title: Ghana to Deploy Condom Vending Machines Nationwide by End of 2026 to Strengthen HIV Prevention
articles.summary: The Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC) has announced plans to install condom vending machines across the country by the end of 2026 as part of efforts to reduce new HIV infections and improve access to sexual health services. The initiative is expected to make condoms more accessible, reduce the stigma associated with purchasing them, and strengthen the country's HIV prevention strategy.

content.html:
Ghana is set to take another significant step in its fight against HIV/AIDS with the nationwide deployment of condom vending machines by the end of 2026, according to the Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC).

The machines will be installed at strategic public locations, including transport terminals, shopping centres, tertiary institutions, entertainment venues, and other high-traffic areas. By making condoms available around the clock, health authorities hope to remove barriers that discourage people from practising safe sex.

The initiative comes at a time when Ghana continues to make progress in reducing HIV infections but still faces a considerable public health challenge. Current estimates indicate that more than 337,000 people are living with HIV in the country. Although new infections have declined in recent years, nearly 14,000 new cases are still recorded annually, underscoring the need for stronger prevention measures.

Health officials estimate that dozens of people contract HIV every day in Ghana. Young people remain among the most vulnerable, with individuals between the ages of 15 and 24 accounting for a significant proportion of new infections. Women also continue to be disproportionately affected, representing nearly two-thirds of people living with the virus.

The Ghana AIDS Commission believes expanding access to condoms remains one of the most effective ways to reduce HIV transmission, alongside regular testing, early treatment, comprehensive sexual health education, and increased public awareness. Officials argue that making condoms readily available through vending machines could encourage more people to adopt safer sexual practices.

Another key objective of the programme is to tackle the social stigma associated with buying condoms. Many people, particularly young adults, avoid purchasing them because they fear being judged. articles.summary: Students of the Krobo Nursing and Midwifery Training College in the Techiman North District have staged a protest over what they describe as poor food quality and deteriorating living conditions. Images of meals allegedly served at the college have sparked widespread public debate, with students demanding improvements in their welfare and the removal of the

content.html:
Students of the Krobo Nursing and Midwifery Training College have taken to the streets to protest against what they describe as poor feeding, inadequate welfare, and administrative challenges at the institution.


The demonstration followed growing dissatisfaction among students, who claim that the meals served at the college are of poor quality and insufficient despite the fees they pay for feeding. Images circulating on social media, reportedly showing some of the meals provided to students, have intensified public discussion about conditions at the institution.


Beyond concerns about food, the protesting students have raised several additional grievances. They allege that they have been deprived of essential learning materials they paid for, including textbooks and medical equipment.

They also complained about the cancellation of breakfast, limited access to potable water, and inadequate library services, arguing that these issues are affecting both their health and academic performance.


According to the students, repeated attempts to have their concerns addressed through internal channels yielded little response, prompting them to stage the demonstration.

They submitted a petition calling for the removal or transfer of the college's principal, accusing the administration of poor leadership, lack of transparency, and mismanagement.


The protest attracted a heavy security presence as police officers were deployed to maintain law and order while students marched peacefully and presented their grievances to the relevant authorities.


The incident has reignited national discussions about student welfare in Ghana's nursing and midwifery training institutions.

Many observers have called on the Ministry of Health and other relevant authorities to investigate the allegations and ensure that students receive nutritious meals, adequate learning resources, and a conducive environment for their training.


As of the time of writing, the college's management had not publicly responded in detail to the specific allegations made by the students. However, many stakeholders are urging dialogue between management and the student body to resolve the issues and restore normal academic activities.


The protest highlights the growing importance of student welfare in tertiary institutions, particularly those responsible for training the country's future healthcare professionals.

Many believe that ensuring quality nutrition and a supportive learning environment is essential to producing competent nurses and midwives capable of delivering quality healthcare across Ghana.

articles.title: Supreme Court Rules Against Delegate System in Political Party Primaries
articles.summary: In a landmark 5 to 2 majority decision, Ghana's Supreme Court has ruled that political parties can no longer rely on the delegate system to elect their presidential and parliamentary candidates. Instead, all registered party members in good standing must be allowed to vote in internal elections, a decision that could significantly reshape the country's political landscape

content.html:
Ghana's Supreme Court has delivered a historic judgment that is expected to transform the way political parties conduct their internal elections.

In a 5 to 2 majority ruling, the Court held that the delegate system used by political parties to elect presidential and parliamentary candidates should no longer be used. The judges ruled that every registered member of a political party who is in good standing must be given the opportunity to vote in these internal contests.

For many years, Ghana's major political parties, including the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and the National Democratic Congress (NDC), have selected their flagbearers and parliamentary candidates through a delegate system. Under this arrangement, only selected party officials and delegates were permitted to vote on behalf of the wider membership.

The Supreme Court found that this approach does not fully reflect the democratic principles enshrined in Ghana's Constitution. As a result, political parties will now have to allow their ordinary members to participate directly in choosing parliamentary candidates and presidential flagbearers.

The ruling is expected to bring significant changes to Ghana's political system. Political parties will have to amend their constitutions, revise their electoral guidelines, and update their voter registers to comply with the Court's decision. Future internal elections are also expected to involve far more participants than in previous years.

Many political observers believe the judgment will strengthen internal democracy by giving grassroots members a stronger voice in deciding who leads their parties. They argue that it will reduce the influence of a small group of delegates and make the selection process more transparent and representative.

At the same time, the decision presents new challenges. Organising nationwide primaries involving all registered members will require greater financial resources, stronger logistics, and improved electoral systems. Political parties will also need to educate their members on the new voting process once the ruling takes effect.

The Supreme Court is expected to release its full written judgment in the coming weeks, providing detailed legal reasons for its decision and guidance on how political parties should implement the new system.

The ruling is already being described as one of the most important constitutional decisions affecting Ghana's democratic process since the country returned to multi-party rule in 1992. It is expected to reshape internal party elections and expand the role of ordinary members in selecting the nation's future political leaders.

articles.title: Supreme Court Unanimously Dismisses Case Challenging OSP's Prosecutorial Powers
articles.summary: Ghana's Supreme Court has unanimously dismissed a constitutional case challenging the prosecutorial powers of the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP). The ruling affirms the OSP's authority to investigate and prosecute corruption-related offences, reinforcing its role in the country's anti-corruption efforts.

content.html:
Ghana's Supreme Court has unanimously dismissed a case that sought to challenge the prosecutorial powers of the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP), delivering a significant victory for the country's anti-corruption framework.

The case questioned whether the OSP had the constitutional authority to independently prosecute corruption and corruption-related offences. However, in a unanimous decision, the apex court rejected the challenge, effectively upholding the powers granted to the Office under the Office of the Special Prosecutor Act.

The ruling strengthens the legal foundation of the OSP, an independent state institution established to investigate, prosecute, and prevent corruption involving public officials and other persons. Since its creation, the Office has played a central role in several high-profile investigations and has often found itself at the centre of legal and political debates.

Legal experts say the Supreme Court's decision provides greater certainty about the OSP's mandate and is likely to remove doubts about its ability to pursue corruption cases without interference. The judgment is also expected to reinforce public confidence in the institution as it continues its work.

The decision comes at a time when the Office of the Special Prosecutor is handling a number of high-profile investigations involving allegations of corruption, abuse of public office, and financial misconduct. Observers believe the ruling could accelerate some of these cases by settling an important constitutional question.

Supporters of the judgment argue that it demonstrates the judiciary's commitment to strengthening institutions established to promote accountability and transparency. Others believe it sends a strong signal that Ghana's legal framework supports independent anti-corruption bodies in carrying out their constitutional responsibilities.

The Office of the Special Prosecutor welcomed the decision, describing it as an important affirmation of its mandate. The full judgment is expected to provide further legal clarity on the constitutional basis of the OSP's prosecutorial authority.

The ruling is widely regarded as a landmark decision in Ghana's ongoing efforts to combat corruption and strengthen the rule of law.

Source: Supreme Court of Ghana / Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP)

articles.title: Techiman Krobo Nursing Training College Closed Indefinitely Following Student Protest
articles.summary: The Krobo Nursing and Midwifery Training College in Techiman has been closed indefinitely following days of unrest over student welfare and feeding conditions. The decision came after an intervention by the Ministry of Health, with the Techiman Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) and the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) holding discussions with students and school authorities in an effort to restore calm.

content.html:
The Krobo Nursing and Midwifery Training College has been shut down indefinitely following the recent student protest over poor feeding and welfare conditions.

The closure comes after tensions escalated on campus during demonstrations, with reports indicating that some students were arrested while others allegedly sustained injuries during an operation by security personnel to restore order. The developments sparked widespread public concern and renewed calls for a peaceful resolution to the crisis.

In response, the Ministry of Health stepped in to address the situation. Acting on behalf of the Ministry, officials engaged the Techiman Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) and officers from the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) to meet with students and the school's management.

The meeting, which lasted several hours, sought to de-escalate tensions, listen to the concerns raised by students, and find a lasting solution to the dispute. Students had earlier complained about the quality of meals served on campus, inadequate welfare, and other conditions they believed were affecting their academic life.

Despite the extensive discussions, authorities ultimately decided to close the institution until further notice. The temporary shutdown is intended to restore calm, ensure the safety of students and staff, and create an environment where the issues raised can be addressed without further disruption.

Students have been directed to vacate the campus while the Ministry of Health and other stakeholders continue their assessment of the situation. It is expected that further engagements will take place before a decision is made on when academic activities can safely resume.

The closure marks a significant development in a dispute that has attracted national attention and reignited conversations about student welfare in Ghana's nursing and midwifery training institutions. Many stakeholders are now urging dialogue, transparency, and meaningful reforms to prevent similar incidents in the future.

Published by Orpheus Grant-Essilfie

articles.title: The Great Reversal: Unpacking the Court of Appeal’s Stunning Acquittal of Former MASLOC CEO Sedina Tamakloe By Orpheus Grant-Essilfie
articles.summary: On July 30, 2026, the Court of Appeal unanimously acquitted and discharged Sedina Tamakloe-Attionu, the former CEO of the Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC). In a 94-page judgment, the appellate court completely overturned her April 2024 High Court conviction and 10-year prison sentence. The judges ruled that the prosecution failed to prove the charges of stealing and causing financial loss to the state beyond a reasonable doubt, and determined that the trial court had lost sight of the fundamental presumption of innocence. This dramatic legal reversal comes just weeks after her high-profile extradition from the United States back to Ghana.

content.html:
The morning of Thursday, July 30, 2026, began like any other typical day in the bustling corridors of Ghana’s judicial system. But by the close of the day, a legal earthquake had rattled the nation. In a stunning reversal that has left political commentators, legal scholars, and the general public deeply astonished, the Court of Appeal unanimously acquitted and discharged Sedina Christine Tamakloe-Attionu, the former Chief Executive Officer of the Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC).

This was no ordinary judicial decision. Just weeks earlier, Tamakloe-Attionu had been dramatically extradited from the United States to Ghana to serve a staggering 10-year prison sentence. Her arrival at Kotoka International Airport on June 9, 2026, surrounded by heavily armed security details, was broadcast live across the country and hailed as a monumental, historic victory for the state's anti-corruption machinery. She was the face of absolute accountability—a high-profile fugitive brought home across the globe to face the music.

And yet, in a meticulously detailed 94-page judgment, the appellate court completely quashed her April 2024 High Court conviction. The decision wiped away all 78 counts of stealing, causing financial loss to the state, conspiracy, money laundering, and procurement-related offenses.

To understand how a case that took nearly seven years to build, prosecute, and culminate in a historic international extradition was completely dismantled in a single afternoon, we have to look far beyond the headlines. We need to take a deep dive into the origins of the MASLOC saga, the grueling trial held in her absence, the high-stakes diplomatic extradition, and the fundamental pillars of criminal justice that the Court of Appeal ruled were fundamentally breached. Let's unpack the entire saga from the beginning, exploring the allegations, the trial, the dramatic escape, and the legal reasoning that led to this monumental acquittal.

The Genesis: What is MASLOC and Who is Sedina Tamakloe?

To fully grasp the magnitude of the allegations that rocked the nation, it is essential to first understand the institution at the center of the storm. The Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC) is a critical state agency in Ghana. Its primary mandate is to provide micro and small loans to start-ups, small businesses, and market women, effectively serving as a financial lifeline for the informal sector and vulnerable entrepreneurs who cannot access traditional banking credit.

Sedina Christine Tamakloe-Attionu took the helm of MASLOC as its Chief Executive Officer in November 2013, serving under the administration of former President John Dramani Mahama. For just over three years, until January 2017, she was responsible for the overall supervision, management, and day-to-day administration of the agency's vast funds, a role that placed immense trust and financial power in her hands.

When political power changed hands following the December 2016 general elections, a new administration took over the reins of government. In 2017, the newly appointed MASLOC CEO, Stephen Amoah, immediately ordered a forensic audit into the operations of his predecessor. Amoah cited numerous irregularities, empty coffers, and highly questionable procurement contracts that had seemingly bypassed standard financial controls and left the agency in a precarious position.

This audit was officially handed over to the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO), which launched a massive, multi-year investigation into Tamakloe-Attionu's tenure. What EOCO investigators unveiled formed the bedrock of a sprawling charge sheet that would eventually feature 78 individual counts of financial malfeasance totaling over GH¢129.5 million (approximately $6 million USD).

A Deep Dive into the 78 Charges

The state's case against Tamakloe-Attionu, and her co-accused, former Operations Manager Daniel Axim, was not based on a single act of theft, but rather a complex web of alleged schemes. The prosecution grouped the 78 charges into several distinct thematic buckets, each representing a different aspect of alleged public sector corruption. Let's break down the core pillars of the prosecution's case.

Allegation CategoryDescription of the Alleged CrimeKey Figures Involved
The Obaatanpa Microfinance SagaA GH¢500,000 investment made by MASLOC that was allegedly refunded in cash due to exorbitant interest demands, but never made it back into MASLOC's accounts.Sedina Tamakloe, Seth Obugyei (Obaatanpa Board), Francis Bandoh (MASLOC Finance)
The Mac Autos ProcurementA single-source contract for 350 vehicles (Chevy Aveo, Sparklite, Isuzu buses) with heavily inflated unit prices, bypassing the Public Procurement Authority (PPA).Sedina Tamakloe, Mac Autos & Spare Parts Ltd, Ministry of Finance, PPA
Kantamanto Fire Victims FundAlleged misappropriation of GH¢1.46 million in relief funds directed by the President to assist victims of the devastating 2013 Kantamanto market fire.Sedina Tamakloe, Daniel Axim
PINCO Project & Ex-GratiaUnauthorized purchase of 200 Samsung phones and arbitrary, unapproved ex-gratia payments paid to the CEO and her deputy upon leaving office.Sedina Tamakloe, Mustapha Batalima (Deputy)

1. The Obaatanpa Cash in a "Ghana Must Go" Bag

One of the most cinematic and heavily contested allegations in the entire trial involved Obaatanpa Microfinance Limited. According to court records and testimonies, MASLOC issued an Agricultural Development Bank (ADB) cheque for GH¢500,000 as an investment in Obaatanpa on July 24, 2014. However, the state alleged that shortly after the cheque was received, Tamakloe-Attionu demanded a staggering 24% interest rate on the investment—a rate so high that Obaatanpa deemed it unprofitable and decided to return the principal.

During the trial, a star witness for the prosecution, Seth Obugyei, testified that when Obaatanpa attempted to return the money via a formal cheque, Tamakloe-Attionu insisted on receiving the refund in cash. Obugyei told the court that he physically handed over GH¢500,000 in cash, stuffed into a checkered 'Ghana Must Go' bag, to the accused at a filling station on the Spintex Road in Accra. The prosecution argued this money was never deposited back into MASLOC's accounts, effectively meaning it was stolen by the CEO.

To corroborate this, Francis Bandoh, the Head of the Finance Unit at MASLOC, testified that he routinely wrote to Obaatanpa on a quarterly basis requesting the payment of interest on the GH¢500,000 investment, completely unaware that the principal had allegedly been returned in cash. Bandoh testified that Obaatanpa never responded to these requests, and when he pressed Tamakloe-Attionu about it, she allegedly brushed it off, claiming it was a "special project" she was handling directly.

2. The Mac Autos Fleet and Massive Price Inflation

The most financially damaging allegation related to procurement irregularities. In December 2016, during the transition period of the government, Tamakloe-Attionu signed a contract with Mac Autos and Spare Parts Limited to supply 350 vehicles intended to be sold on a hire-purchase arrangement to the Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU).

The state prosecutors alleged that this massive contract was executed without the mandatory approval from the Public Procurement Authority (PPA). More damningly, the state alleged massive price inflation that cost the taxpayer millions.

The fallout from this contract was immediate and severe. When the new MASLOC CEO, Stephen Amoah, took over, he discovered that the vehicles were rotting in parking lots. The GPRTU drivers had flatly refused to purchase the vehicles because the hire-purchase terms, based on the inflated base prices, were completely unaffordable. The state argued that this deliberate inflation, coupled with the bypassing of the PPA, constituted a willful causing of financial loss to the state.

3. The Kantamanto Fire and Sensitization Funds

In 2013, a devastating fire ripped through the Kantamanto market in Accra, destroying the livelihoods of thousands of informal traders. In response to the tragedy, the government released GH¢1.46 million to MASLOC to disburse as urgent relief to the victims. EOCO investigations, however, claimed that Tamakloe-Attionu personally appropriated over GH¢579,800 of these highly sensitive funds, diverting money meant for desperate fire victims into private pockets.

Furthermore, the state alleged that millions of cedis were repeatedly withdrawn for nationwide "sensitization and monitoring" exercises that largely never took place. According to the charge sheet, Tamakloe-Attionu and Axim withdrew GH¢1,816,000 in tranches for these phantom exercises, despite the MASLOC board only approving a lesser sum, and pocketed the difference alongside GH¢246,280 meant for financial literacy training.

4. Unauthorized Ex-Gratia and the PINCO Project

As she was leaving office in January 2017, the state alleged that Tamakloe-Attionu authorized the payment of GH¢135,592 to herself and GH¢82,218 to her deputy, Mustapha Abubakar Batalima, as ex-gratia payments. Prosecutors argued these payments were made entirely without board approval or legal authorization, treating the state coffers as a personal severance fund. Additionally, in November 2016, MASLOC procured 200 Samsung B310 mobile phones under a project called the PINCO Project Market Survey, which the state also flagged as an unauthorized and irregular procurement.

The Long Road to Trial and the Great Escape

In January 2019, the Attorney General officially filed the 78 charges at the Accra High Court. Tamakloe-Attionu and Daniel Axim pleaded not guilty to all charges, which included stealing, money laundering, and willfully causing financial loss to the state. Given the severity of the charges, she was granted bail to the tune of GH¢5 million with two sureties. These sureties were not ordinary citizens; they included prominent figures like Alex Mould, the former CEO of the National Petroleum Authority, and Gavivina Tamakloe.

For the first two years, the trial proceeded through the normal, albeit slow, gears of the Ghanaian justice system. The prosecution paraded its witnesses, presenting audit reports, financial statements, and oral testimonies to paint a picture of a CEO who treated the state agency's treasury as a personal slush fund. The defense cross-examined witnesses, and the state painstakingly built its case.

But in February 2021, the narrative took a sharp and dramatic turn. Claiming she required specialized medical attention, Tamakloe-Attionu sought and was granted permission by the High Court to travel to the United States for a medical check-up. Her passport, which had been held tightly by the court as a primary condition of her bail, was released to her.

She boarded a flight to the United States—and simply did not return.

Months turned into years. The court repeatedly issued warrants for her arrest and aggressively summoned her high-profile sureties to explain her whereabouts. In a dramatic twist in January 2023, the court ordered Alex Mould and Gavivina Tamakloe to pay the GH¢5 million bail bond to the state because they could not produce the accused, threatening to freeze and liquidate their properties if they failed to pay the massive sum.

The Mechanics of a Trial In Absentia

When a high-profile defendant flees a criminal trial, the justice system faces a philosophical and procedural crisis. Does the trial grind to a halt, effectively rewarding the fugitive for their escape? Or does it continue, risking the violation of the defendant's fundamental constitutional right to be present, to face their accusers, and to defend themselves?

In Ghana, Article 19(3) of the 1992 Constitution guarantees an accused person the absolute right to be present at their trial. However, the law provides very narrow, specific exceptions. Justice Afia Serwaa Asare-Botwe, a highly respected Court of Appeal judge sitting with additional responsibilities as a High Court judge, had a critical decision to make.

On January 23, 2023, Justice Asare-Botwe made a definitive ruling: Tamakloe-Attionu had intentionally disabled herself from the opportunity to be tried in her presence. The judge noted that the accused was well aware of the pending charges and the gravity of the trial, having actively participated in the proceedings for over a year before absconding. The court outlined that a trial in absentia is permitted if a person refuses to attend after being informed, or if their behavior is so disruptive that the trial cannot proceed.

To satisfy the constitutional requirements of notice, the court ordered that notices of the decision be published in national newspapers and posted at her last known residence, effectively providing formal legal notice, and allowed the trial to proceed in absentia.

The trial pressed on without her physical presence. Her co-accused, Daniel Axim, was left to face the music alone in the courtroom, bearing the full brunt of the state's prosecutorial machinery.

The April 2024 Conviction

On April 16, 2024, Justice Asare-Botwe delivered her highly anticipated judgment. Relying heavily on the documentary evidence provided by EOCO, the three-tier test for causing financial loss, and flatly rejecting the defense of "superior orders" raised by Daniel Axim (who claimed he was merely following the CEO's instructions), the judge found both defendants guilty.

Sedina Tamakloe-Attionu was convicted on over 70 counts and sentenced to 10 years in prison in absentia. Daniel Axim, present in court, was sentenced to 5 years. Consider the GH¢500,000 cash allegedly handed over in the 'Ghana Must Go' bag. While a witness testified to handing over the cash, proving that the money was subsequently
stolen

or intentionally misappropriated by the accused—rather than routed through informal operational channels, used for legitimate but poorly documented agency expenses, or lost to systemic institutional failures—requires irrefutable proof of personal enrichment or deliberate financial sabotage.

The appellate court essentially determined that the state's narrative, while perhaps highly suspicious, was fraught with evidentiary holes. Suspicion, no matter how deep, cannot substitute for hard evidence. The prosecution's failure to definitively close these evidentiary gaps meant that reasonable doubt persisted, mandating an acquittal.
2. The Presumption of Innocence and the Psychology of Flight
The second, and perhaps most philosophically fascinating reason for the acquittal, involved the trial judge's handling of the constitutional "presumption of innocence".
The Court of Appeal boldly stated that the trial judge, Justice Asare-Botwe, "lost sight of the presumption of innocence until proven guilty".
This critique gets to the heart of the psychological difficulty inherent in a trial
in absentia

. When a defendant asks for their passport to seek medical care, leaves the country, and then blatantly refuses to return for three years while their trial proceeds, it is human nature to view that flight as a tacit admission of guilt. In common parlance, "only the guilty run." It is incredibly difficult for any adjudicator to look at an empty defendant's chair and not feel a sense of defiance and inherent guilt radiating from it.
However, in jurisprudence, flight does not equate to guilt. The Ghanaian Constitution demands that an accused person be presumed innocent until the very moment a guilty verdict is pronounced based
solely
on the evidence presented in court, completely divorced from their post-charge behavior.

The appellate court's ruling strongly suggests that the trial court allowed the defendant's deliberate abscondment to color its assessment of the evidence. When a judge subconsciously views a fleeing defendant as already guilty, they may unconsciously lower the evidentiary bar required for the prosecution to secure a conviction. The Court of Appeal reasserted that regardless of how defiant, evasive, or disrespectful a defendant behaves toward the judicial process, the state must still flawlessly prove every single element of the crime. The appellate panel found that this fundamental constitutional protection had been dangerously compromised in the lower court.
3. Prosecutorial Missteps and Case Handling
Finally, the Court of Appeal heavily faulted the specific manner in which the prosecution handled the case from its inception.

In complex white-collar crimes involving state procurement (such as the Mac Autos deal) and executive ex-gratia payments, prosecutors must carefully navigate a labyrinth of administrative law, corporate governance, and criminal statutes. A bad business decision, or even a negligent failure to secure PPA approval, does not automatically equate to the criminal intent required for "willfully causing financial loss to the state."

If the prosecution relies too heavily on hearsay, fails to call material witnesses to corroborate the movement of funds, or introduces documents without establishing a proper, unshakeable foundation, an appellate court will strike that evidence from the record. Furthermore, charging a defendant with 78 distinct counts can sometimes be a double-edged sword. While it highlights the massive scale of the alleged corruption to the public, it also exponentially increases the burden on the prosecution in the courtroom. They must prove 78 distinct criminal acts without a single fatal error. The appellate court’s ruling implies that the state’s strategy was overzealous, disorganized, or legally unsound, relying on the sheer volume of charges rather than the undeniable weight of the evidence.
Second and Third-Order Implications: The Ripple Effects of the Acquittal

A ruling of this magnitude does not happen in a vacuum. The shockwaves of Sedina Tamakloe-Attionu's acquittal will be felt across multiple domains of Ghanaian society—from the political arena to international diplomatic channels—for years to come. By analyzing the underlying dynamics, we can extract several critical insights into the broader implications of this case.
1. The Fate of Daniel Axim and Accomplice Liability

The most immediate ripple effect concerns Daniel Axim, the former Operations Manager of MASLOC who was sentenced to 5 years in prison alongside his former boss. Axim had already appealed his conviction and was remarkably granted bail by the Supreme Court in January 2026 pending the outcome of that appeal.

In criminal law, the fate of an accomplice is often inextricably linked to the principal actor, especially in conspiracy charges. If the Court of Appeal has ruled that the prosecution failed to prove that the core crimes of stealing and causing financial loss actually occurred, the legal foundation for Axim's conviction instantly crumbles. One cannot conspire to commit a crime that the court has determined was not proven to exist. Axim’s legal team is now virtually guaranteed to secure his complete exoneration based on this appellate precedent.
2. A Crushing Blow to the Attorney General and EOCO
For the ruling administration and the Attorney General’s Office, July 30, 2026, represents a catastrophic legal and public relations defeat.

The state invested immense resources into this case over nearly a decade. EOCO spent years conducting forensic audits. State attorneys spent five grueling years litigating the case in the High Court. The government expended significant diplomatic capital to secure the first US-Ghana extradition in 17 years, coordinating intensely with the US Department of Justice, the FBI, and the US Marshals.

To achieve the absolute pinnacle of international legal cooperation—physically dragging a fugitive across the globe to face justice—only to have the domestic appellate court declare that the prosecution failed to do its basic job is a deeply embarrassing scenario for the state. It raises severe, uncomfortable questions about the competence of the prosecutorial strategy and the rigor of EOCO's initial investigations. Critics will undoubtedly argue that the state engaged in a highly publicized political witch-hunt without securing the foundational evidence necessary to sustain a conviction under rigorous appellate scrutiny.
3. The Extradition Treaty and International Relations

One of the fascinating third-order effects of this ruling involves international diplomacy. When Ghana requested Tamakloe-Attionu's extradition, the United States reviewed the evidence. A US District Court judge in Nevada reviewed the High Court conviction, assessed the charges to ensure dual criminality, and certified that she should be handed over.

On a superficial level, the swift acquittal upon her return might look bizarre to international observers. Why go through the massive effort of extradition just to let her go? However, from a diplomatic and legal standpoint, this acquittal actually serves as a profound, undeniable validation of the independence of the Ghanaian judiciary.

The US State Department, European nations, and international human rights bodies are often highly hesitant to extradite individuals to developing nations out of fear that the judicial system might be a mere rubber stamp for executive vengeance. By overturning the conviction of a high-profile political opponent of the ruling government, the Court of Appeal has boldly signaled to the global community that Ghana’s appellate courts operate entirely free from executive influence. It proves that the system of checks and balances functions correctly, even when the political optics are highly inconvenient for the ruling government. This could paradoxically make future extradition requests by Ghana much
easier
to approve, as international courts now have concrete proof of Ghana’s robust judicial independence.
4. The Political Theater and Public Perception
In the court of public opinion, legal nuance often takes a backseat to narrative. For the average Ghanaian citizen, the narrative is perplexing and potentially infuriating.

The public witnessed an audit that claimed GH¢129 million was lost. They saw a CEO flee the country during a trial. They saw her extradited in handcuffs, paraded as a victory for the taxpayer. To suddenly be told that she is an innocent woman because the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt will trigger widespread cynicism about the justice system's ability to hold the elite accountable.

The political climate in Ghana is currently hyper-charged. Concurrently, high-profile figures like Chairman Wontumi are engaged in their own massive legal battles and appeals, highlighting a society heavily focused on the intersection of law and politics.

The opposition National Democratic Congress (NDC), of which Tamakloe-Attionu is a prominent member, will likely frame this as the ultimate proof of political persecution and a complete vindication of their tenure at MASLOC. Conversely, anti-corruption activists may view this as a tragic technical failure of the justice system, where a well-resourced defendant exploited procedural and prosecutorial errors to escape accountability. The truth, buried in 94 pages of legal jargon, will likely be twisted to fit competing political narratives ahead of future elections.
5. What Happens Next? The Supreme Court Looms

The story does not necessarily end here. In Ghana's tiered judicial system, the state has the constitutional right to appeal the Court of Appeal's decision to the highest court of the land: the Supreme Court.

Given the sheer amount of political capital invested in this case, and the deep embarrassment of the July 30 acquittal, it is highly probable that the Attorney General will file an appeal to the Supreme Court. However, overturning an appellate acquittal is notoriously difficult. The Supreme Court is generally deferential to lower courts on findings of fact. The state will have to prove that the Court of Appeal committed fundamental errors in law when evaluating the trial judge's application of the presumption of innocence and the burden of proof.

If the state appeals, Tamakloe-Attionu will find herself once again fighting for her freedom in the nation's apex court. But for now, the reality of the situation is stark. As of the evening of July 30, 2026, Sedina Tamakloe-Attionu is a free woman, unanimously acquitted and discharged of all charges, her 10-year prison sentence nothing but a memory.

This saga is destined to become a staple in Ghanaian legal textbooks. It features every element of a legal thriller: massive financial sums, a brazen flight from justice, complex international extradition, and a sudden, dramatic acquittal. But beyond the drama, the July 30, 2026, Court of Appeal judgment serves as a profound reminder of the harsh realities of the criminal justice system. It reinforces the ancient legal doctrine formulated by the English jurist William Blackstone:
“It is better that ten guilty persons escape than that one innocent suffer.”

The appellate court’s ruling is not necessarily a declaration that no money was lost at MASLOC, nor is it a blind endorsement of Tamakloe-Attionu’s tenure. Rather, it is a strict, unyielding policing of the state's power. It sends a chilling message to prosecutors and trial judges alike: no matter how high-profile the defendant, no matter how egregious their behavior during the trial, and no matter how loud the public outcry for a conviction, the state must meticulously, flawlessly, and incontrovertibly prove its case. When the state fails to do so, the scales of justice demand an acquittal. And in this historic case, against all odds and public expectation, the scales tipped entirely in favor of Sedina Tamakloe

articles.title: BANK OF GHANA INJECTED NEARLY $13 BILLION INTO FOREX MARKET IN JUST ONE YEAR, IMF REVEALS
articles.summary: The IMF says the Bank of Ghana injected nearly $13 billion into the foreign exchange market over one year to stabilize the cedi during Ghana's economic recovery. While the interventions helped restore confidence, the Fund says they should gradually give way to a more market-driven exchange rate supported by transparent and predictable central bank operations.

content.html:
Currency interventions by central banks are not unusual. They are often used to ease sharp swings in exchange rates, calm market uncertainty, and ensure businesses can access foreign currency when demand suddenly rises. In Ghana's case, the IMF believes those interventions played an important role in supporting macroeconomic stability as the country worked through its economic recovery programme.


At the same time, the Fund argues that such large-scale support cannot become a permanent strategy. A market that depends too heavily on central bank intervention may struggle to reflect the true forces of supply and demand. Over time, that can discourage a more competitive and transparent foreign exchange market.

Rather than criticizing the interventions outright, the IMF's assessment strikes a balance. It acknowledges that the Bank of Ghana acted during an exceptional period, while encouraging a gradual shift toward a system where the market plays a greater role in determining exchange rates and the central bank intervenes only when necessary.

The Fund also welcomed the Bank of Ghana's efforts to introduce a more structured foreign exchange operations framework. A clearer set of rules, it noted, can make interventions more predictable, improve transparency, and strengthen confidence among investors and market participants.

The disclosure comes as Ghana continues to implement reforms under its IMF-supported programme. Inflation has eased compared with previous highs, foreign exchange reserves have improved, and confidence in the economy has gradually strengthened. Even so, the IMF maintains that sustaining these gains will depend on disciplined monetary policy, prudent fiscal management, and a foreign exchange market that becomes increasingly resilient without heavy and continuous central bank support.

articles.title: ACCRA BROUGHT TO A STANDSTILL AS NPP STAGES MASSIVE PROTEST
articles.summary: Thousands march against alleged selective justice and what the party describes as growing threats to Ghana's democracy

content.html:
The streets of Accra were filled with thousands of supporters of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) as the party staged one of its biggest demonstrations this year. The protest, held under the theme "Democracy Under Attack," drew party executives, Members of Parliament, former government officials, grassroots supporters, and sympathizers from across the country.



From the early hours of the day, major roads leading into the capital experienced heavy traffic as demonstrators, dressed largely in red, black, and party colours, converged to begin the march. Chanting patriotic songs, waving placards, and carrying Ghanaian flags, protesters insisted they were defending democratic principles rather than pursuing partisan interests.

At the heart of the demonstration is the NPP's claim that state institutions are increasingly being used to target political opponents. Party leaders argue that recent arrests, prosecutions, and investigations involving members of the opposition point to a worrying pattern of selective justice. They maintain that the rule of law must apply equally to every Ghanaian, regardless of political affiliation.

The party also contends that freedom of expression is under pressure. According to its leadership, criticism of government policies should not expose citizens, journalists, activists, or political opponents to intimidation or legal action. These concerns have become a central part of the NPP's recent political messaging, with party officials repeatedly calling for stronger protection of constitutional rights.

Throughout the march, demonstrators displayed placards bearing messages demanding fairness, judicial independence, and respect for democratic institutions. Organisers described the protest as a peaceful exercise of constitutional rights and urged supporters to remain disciplined while making their concerns known.


The demonstration comes at a time of heightened political tension in Ghana, with legal battles involving several high-profile political figures continuing to dominate national discussions. Against that backdrop, today's protest has become more than a party event. It has evolved into a broader political statement about governance, accountability, and the direction of Ghana's democracy.


As proceedings continue, security personnel remain deployed across key locations in the capital to maintain order and ensure the march proceeds peacefully. More statements from political leaders and state institutions are expected as the demonstration unfolds.

articles.title: Jorge Messi, Father of Soccer Legend Lionel Messi, Passes Away at 68
articles.summary: Jorge Messi, the father and long-time agent of soccer superstar Lionel Messi, has died at the age of 68 after a long illness.

content.html:
It is a very sad day for the soccer world. Jorge Messi, the father of soccer superstar Lionel Messi, has passed away at the age of 68.


​Jorge died at 10 p.m. on August 7, 2026, in a hospital in his hometown of Rosario, Argentina. He had been fighting a long illness.
​If you followed the 2026 World Cup this summer, you might remember some major drama on the news.

A TV reporter wrongly announced that Jorge had died. That fake news caused a lot of pain, and the reporter even quit her job because of the massive mistake. At the time, the Messi family let everyone know Jorge was just sick and getting medical care.

Lionel even cried on the field after scoring three goals against Algeria, explaining later that he was going through a tough time with his family.

Sadly, this time the news of his passing is completely real.
​Jorge was so much more than just a dad.

He was the main reason Lionel had such an amazing career. When Lionel was a little boy with a medical condition that stopped him from growing, Jorge worked hard to make sure he got the expensive treatments he needed.

When a 13-year-old Lionel got the chance to play for Barcelona, Jorge packed up and moved across the world to Spain to protect and guide him.


​For Lionel's entire life, Jorge stayed quietly in the background. He rarely gave interviews, but he was always in charge behind the scenes.

He acted as his son's official agent, handling the big contracts, dealing with sports brands, and managing the business side of things.


​Jorge helped turn a small boy from Argentina into the greatest soccer player in history. He leaves behind his wife, four children, and an incredible legacy.

articles.title: Great APASS Gets Top Honors: Apam SHS Officially Upgraded to Category A
articles.summary: Apam Senior High School has officially been upgraded to a Category A school. Great APASS grew from a tiny cocoa shed into one of Ghana's top educational powerhouses.

content.html:
The government has officially upgraded the school to Category A. This means the Ghana Education Service now recognizes it as one of the very best high schools in the entire country.

While the students and teachers are celebrating this huge win today, the school, proudly known as "Great APASS," did not start at the top. Its story is actually very inspiring.

Apam SHS opened its doors on February 20, 1953. It was started by the late Rev. J.W. DeGraft-Johnson. Back then, there was no massive campus or modern buildings.

The very first 20 students took their classes inside a small cocoa shed at a place called Apaa Paado. It started as a simple day school with only two teachers.

By 1960, the school had grown and moved to its beautiful current home, a location known as "Mbofra mfa Adwen".

The famous headmaster Peter Augustus Owiredu took over, and under his strong leadership, people started calling the school "Great APASS". In 1964, the school added boarding houses, which allowed students from all over the country to travel there to learn.

The new Category A status is a well-deserved reward for the school's hard work. The students truly live by their motto, "Obrapa gya owura kwan," which means "Character and Efficiency".

The school has had several headteachers who transformed and helped structure Great APASS. This includes Esther Hamilton, who coined the famous APASS phrase known as "Marketing," which simply means an interaction between a boy and a girl. Consequently, she was followed by leaders like Jemima Atta Elsie Morrison and the current headmistress, Comfort Essah Amoafoh, who is still guiding the school to greater heights.

Recently, their achievements have been nothing short of incredible. The Apam Robotics team made it to the national finals and earned a spot to represent Ghana at a huge World Championship in Michigan, United States.

Their brilliant Science and Maths (NSMQ) team even defeated the famous Mfantsipim Boys SHS to reach the national competition.

The students also get top grades, with some achieving truly historic results. In 2021, an exceptional student named NasiruDeen Ghartey graduated from Apam SHS with a perfect 8 As.

He then went on to the University of Cape Coast, where he recently graduated as the valedictorian with a flawless 4.0 CGPA. His performance was so outstanding that the Acting Vice-Chancellor, Professor Denis Worlanyo Aheto, publicly pledged to personally sponsor his further studies abroad.

Because of its great training, this school has also produced some of Ghana's most important leaders. Top judges like former Chief Justice Kwasi Anin-Yeboah and Supreme Court Justice Nene Amegatcher went to school here.

It is also the former high school of famous politician Aaron Mike Oquaye, rich businessman Nana Kwame Bediako, and popular musician Guru.

From a tiny shed in 1953 to a powerful Category A school today, Great APASS keeps proving why it is one of the best places to learn in Ghana.


Obrapa ! Gya Owura Kwan!

articles.title: Free Speech Under Siege: Martin Kpebu Warns Government Over Rising Arrests
articles.summary: Lawyer Martin Kpebu is speaking out against the recent wave of free speech arrests in Ghana, noting that the Mahama government has made more arrests in 18 months than the previous administration did in eight years.

content.html:
Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu is very upset about the current situation. He recently went on television to share his frustration about the growing number of citizens being locked up just for expressing their opinions.

Kpebu pointed out a very shocking comparison. He stated that the current Mahama administration has arrested more people over free speech in just 18 months than former President Akufo-Addo did during his entire eight years in office.

He reminded everyone that during the previous government, citizens openly called leaders harsh names without being thrown into a police cell. But today, the climate is completely different.

A perfect example of this shift is the arrest of the popular Ghanaian social media influencer known on X (formerly Twitter) as Gen Buhari. Known for being a vocal supporter of the opposition and sharing his strong political opinions online, his arrest yesterday has shocked many internet users.

Sadly, his story is part of a growing trend where the police are targeting social media users and political communicators.

Just a few months ago, an opposition party communicator named Baba Amando was arrested. He was put in handcuffs and driven for eight hours simply because he posted some digitally altered pictures on Facebook.

Another social media user, a TikTok creator named Camilla Alhassan, was also tracked down by the police and remanded in custody just for making claims about the president in a video.

Martin Kpebu says this new strategy of using the police to silence critics is completely wrong. While he agrees that insulting leaders is not a polite thing to do, he firmly believes that arresting citizens is never the right solution.

His advice to the government is very clear: just let the people talk.

He warned that if the government keeps arresting citizens for speaking their minds, they will quickly lose all the goodwill and support of the people.

At the end of the day, harsh words, internet memes, and social media posts do not actually hurt the government. But locking people up for talking definitely hurts Ghana's democracy.

articles.title: World Cup Hero Ferran Torres Nears €50 Million Move to PSG
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain and FC Barcelona are finalizing a massive €50 million transfer deal for Spanish forward and 2026 World Cup hero, Ferran Torres.

content.html:
Have you heard the latest huge soccer transfer news?

Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona are very close to finalizing a massive deal.


​Spanish forward Ferran Torres is getting ready to pack his bags and move to France. The final price tag for this transfer is expected to be around €50 million.


​Why is this happening? Even though Torres is a great player, he has struggled to get consistent playing time in Barcelona's starting lineup.

He wants a fresh start where he can play more often, and he has let the club know that he wants to join PSG.


​Torres is coming off an absolutely unbelievable summer. He recently became a national legend in Spain after he scored the game-winning goal in the 106th minute of the 2026 World Cup final against Argentina.

After that amazing performance on the world's biggest stage, PSG made it a priority to sign him.


​For Barcelona, selling him right now makes perfect financial sense.

Torres only has one year left on his contract. If they do not sell him this summer, he could leave the team for free next year.

By securing this €50 million deal, Barcelona will get a huge cash boost that they desperately need to sign a new striker, like Argentina's Julián Álvarez.


​Right now, Torres has already agreed to his personal contract terms with the French club.

Everyone is just waiting for Barcelona and PSG to sign the final paperwork and make the move officially complete.

articles.title: Police Arrest Two Brothers After Wild Chase for Stealing 30 Goats
articles.summary: Two brothers are in police custody after a hot car chase in the Ashanti Region. They were caught trying to steal 30 goats in a passenger van.

content.html:
Sometimes, the news just makes you shake your head and wonder what people are thinking. It is hard to believe that people would resort to stealing goats instead of finding legitimate work.


​In Sekyedumase, a town in the Ashanti Region, the police recently had to go on a wild car chase to stop two brothers.


​Their crime was bold and bizarre. The brothers allegedly stole about 30 goats.

Instead of using a normal farm truck, they somehow managed to cram all of those live animals into a Toyota Voxy, which is a regular passenger van.


​Seeing a passenger van stuffed full of goats moving through the area obviously looked very suspicious.

The police noticed the strange vehicle and decided to investigate.


​When the brothers realized they were caught, they tried to speed away.

The police went on a hot chase, eventually blocking the van and arresting both suspects.


​Thankfully, all 30 stolen goats were safely recovered.

The two brothers are now in police custody, answering for the bizarre theft.


​This story proves a very simple point.

Taking things that do not belong to you, especially from hardworking farmers, will only land you in serious trouble.

articles.title: Police Arrest Four Suspects After Finding 118 Bags of Hidden Cocoa at Bunkpurugu
articles.summary: Police in the North East Region have arrested four individuals caught trying to smuggle 11,800 kilograms of cocoa beans into Togo by hiding them under plantains.

content.html:
The Ghana Police Service has stopped a major smuggling operation in the North East Region.


​On August 9, 2026, officers at a checkpoint in Bunkpurugu arrested four suspects who were trying to sneak a massive amount of cocoa out of the country.


​The suspects were driving a Hyundai Rhino truck toward the Togo border.

To fool the police, they covered their illegal cargo with a huge load of plantains.​The trick did not work.

The police had received a tip-off about the truck. When they stopped the vehicle, a joint security team conducted a thorough search at the local Customs Office.

They found exactly 118 bags of cocoa beans completely hidden underneath the plantains. All together, the hidden cocoa weighed 11,800 kilograms.


​The four people arrested include the 35-year-old driver, his 19-year-old assistant, a 22-year-old man, and a 23-year-old woman named Ernestina Akugre who claimed she owned the entire shipment.


​The suspects are currently in police custody. The authorities have stated they will be taken to court to face the law for their actions.


​This successful arrest is part of an ongoing national effort by security agencies and COCOBOD to protect Ghana's economy by stopping criminals from illegally transporting valuable cocoa beans into neighboring countries.

articles.title: Attorney General Fights Chairman Wontumi's Request to Leave Prison on Bail
articles.summary: The Attorney General's office is strongly opposing Chairman Wontumi's request to be released on bail, arguing that his appeal against his 20-year prison sentence is unlikely to succeed.

content.html:
The legal battle over the imprisonment of the Ashanti Regional NPP Chairman, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, is getting even more intense.

​Known to most people as Chairman Wontumi, he is currently locked up and serving a 20-year prison sentence. A High Court judge recently found him guilty of facilitating illegal mining, often called galamsey, on a concession at Samreboi in the Western Region.

​His legal team, led by lawyer Samuel Atta Akyea, strongly disagrees with the heavy sentence. They have filed an official appeal, listing over 20 different reasons why they believe the original trial was flawed and unfair.

​Because the appeal process can take a very long time, Wontumi's lawyers filed another special request. They asked the court to grant him bail so he can go home and live his normal life while they fight the case.

​However, the government is doing everything it can to keep him behind bars.

​The Attorney General's office stepped into the courtroom to strongly oppose the bail application. They told the judge that Chairman Wontumi should not be released because his appeal has almost no reasonable chance of actually succeeding.

​From the government's point of view, the original trial proved beyond a doubt that he broke the law. They believe the evidence is rock solid and the 20-year punishment is exactly what he deserves for his role in illegal mining.

​Deputy Attorney-General Dr. Justice Srem-Sai has also publicly defended the government's stance. He has pushed back hard against claims that Wontumi is just a victim of political targeting, reminding everyone that the case is strictly about enforcing the law and protecting the environment.

​Now, all eyes are on the judge.

​The court will have to weigh the arguments from both sides and make a final decision. They will determine if Chairman Wontumi gets to wait for his appeal out on bail, or if he has to stay inside his prison cell.

articles.title: Disaster Avoided: Firefighters Prevent Massive 45,000-Litre Fuel Explosion in Tamale
articles.summary: Heroic firefighters in Tamale successfully rescued two people and prevented a massive explosion after a tanker carrying 45,000 litres of diesel overturned.

content.html:
A team of heroic firefighters just saved the day and prevented what could have been a massive disaster in Tamale.

On Tuesday, a huge fuel tanker completely overturned on the road at Adubili Yili.

This was an incredibly dangerous situation. The truck was carrying about 45,000 litres of highly flammable diesel, making it a ticking time bomb.

The driver and his assistant were trapped inside the wrecked vehicle. Thankfully, crew members from the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) Northern Regional Headquarters rushed to the scene immediately.

The firefighters quickly sprang into action. They successfully pulled the two trapped men out of the truck and handed them over to the National Ambulance Service so they could get urgent medical care.

But the danger was not over yet. Diesel was spilling everywhere.

To stop a deadly fire or a massive explosion from wiping out the area, the fire crew carefully cooled down the tanker and worked hard to contain all the spilled fuel.

Things actually got even more chaotic during the rescue operation. Out of nowhere, two passenger buses collided right next to the accident scene.

One of those buses even slammed into a parked fire truck, damaging its air system.

Amazingly, despite the extra crash and all the chaos, no additional people were hurt in that second accident.

Following this wild rescue, the Fire Service issued a strong warning to all drivers. They are begging motorists to slow down and be extremely careful around accident scenes so emergency workers have enough safe space to do their jobs and save lives.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez Are Officially Married
articles.summary: Football legend Cristiano Ronaldo and his longtime partner Georgina Rodríguez have officially tied the knot in a private wedding ceremony in Portugal.

content.html:
Cristiano Ronaldo is a married man! The football legend has finally tied the knot with his longtime partner, Georgina Rodríguez.

The happy couple got married on August 11, 2026, in a quiet, private civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal. Interestingly, the timing of the wedding is very special. They said their vows exactly one year to the day after announcing their engagement on August 11, 2025.

Shortly after the ceremony, they shared the exciting news with the world on Instagram. The couple posted a sweet picture showing off their new wedding rings with a simple caption that read: "C❤️G". Keeping it a very intimate family event, all five of their children were there to celebrate the special moment with them.

Looking back, the newlyweds have a great love story. They first met in 2016 while Georgina was working at a Gucci store in Madrid, and they have been together ever since.

Leading up to their big day, there was actually a very funny mix-up regarding the wedding. Just a few days before the real ceremony, a wild rumor spread online claiming they were getting married on August 8 at a historic church in Ronaldo's hometown of Madeira. As a result, thousands of excited fans rushed to the church to see the famous couple. However, they ended up accidentally crashing the wedding of a regular local couple! The poor bride and groom had to push their way through a massive crowd just to get to their own ceremony.

Now, after that funny mix-up and nearly a decade of dating, the global football icon and his beautiful bride are finally husband and wife

articles.title: Ghana Spends Over $230 Million a Year on Tomato Imports, Reaches 99% Ginger Dependence
articles.summary: New research shows Ghana spends over $230 million every year importing tomatoes and now relies on other countries for 99% of its ginger after a major plant disease outbreak.

content.html:
According to new research from the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), the numbers are quite shocking. Ghana is currently spending over $230 million every single year on fresh and processed tomato imports.


​Dr. Michael Kwabena Osei, a top researcher at the CSIR, explained that Ghanaians eat a lot of tomatoes.

The country needs over 1.4 million metric tonnes of tomatoes every year, but local farmers are only able to grow about 15 to 18 percent of that massive amount.
​Because of this huge gap, Ghana has to buy fresh tomatoes from neighboring Burkina Faso and rocessed tomato paste from places like China and Europe.


​The story is even worse when it comes to ginger. Right now, Ghana is 99 percent dependent on imported ginger just to meet the needs of its people.


​Just a few years ago, local farmers were growing plenty of it. But in 2022, a terrible plant disease known as the "ginger killer" wiped out almost all of the ginger farms.


​This bacterial outbreak caused local ginger production to drop from over 100 tonnes down to just 10 tonnes.
​Because ginger is so scarce now, the price has skyrocketed. A sack of ginger that used to cost 250 Ghana Cedis in 2022 recently jumped to around 6,000 Cedis.


​So, how can the country fix this expensive problem? The scientists say Ghana needs to invest heavily in its own farming technology.


​Dr. Osei warned that a country that imports all its seeds will always have to import its food.

He suggested creating a special Tomato Board and producing better, disease-resistant seeds for local farmers to plant.


​By focusing on better agricultural science, good irrigation, and healthier soils, researchers believe Ghana can start growing enough food to feed itself and keep millions of dollars inside the country.

articles.title: Attorney General Withdraws Court of Appeal Motion to Keep Sedina Tamakloe in Prison
articles.summary: The Attorney General has officially withdrawn a motion at the Court of Appeal that aimed to stop former MASLOC CEO Sedina Tamakloe from being released. The legal fight has now moved to the Supreme Court.

content.html:
​The legal drama surrounding former MASLOC CEO Sedina Tamakloe just took another interesting turn this morning.

​If you have been following the news, you know that the Court of Appeal recently shocked the nation by overturning her 10-year prison sentence and clearing her of all charges.

​Immediately after she was cleared, the Attorney General's office tried to stop her from going free. They filed a legal request at the Court of Appeal called a "stay of execution" to keep her in prison while they prepared to appeal the final decision.

​However, there is a major breaking update today, August 12, 2026. The Attorney General has officially changed their legal strategy.

​Principal State Attorney Hilda Craig appeared before the Court of Appeal this morning and completely withdrew their application to block her release. Because the government withdrew the request, the court officially struck the motion out.

​But this does not mean the government is giving up on the case. They are just moving the fight to a higher level.

​Instead of arguing at the Court of Appeal, the Attorney General has now taken the battle straight to the highest court in the land. They have filed a brand-new stay of execution directly at the Supreme Court.

​The state is still hoping to keep her behind bars while they fight to get her original 10-year sentence restored. The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear this new motion on October 13, 2026.

​For now, the battle lines have moved, and all eyes will be on the Supreme Court this October to see what happens next.

articles.title: Xavi Hernández Named New Head Coach of the Netherlands
articles.summary: Former Barcelona manager Xavi Hernández has officially agreed to become the new head coach of the Netherlands national football team, and the Dutch football federation has confirmed the deal runs until 2030.

content.html:

The Dutch football federation has now officially confirmed the appointment. They released a public message today to proudly welcome Xavi as their new leader.

According to the official announcement, the final paperwork was signed today. Xavi agreed to a brand-new contract that will keep him in charge of the Dutch squad until the year 2030.

Xavi is stepping in to replace Ronald Koeman. Koeman recently parted ways with the team after the Netherlands was knocked out of the 2026 World Cup.

This is a very exciting move for the football world. Before taking this job, the 46-year-old spent over two years managing Barcelona, where he guided them to a La Liga championship.

Now, he is taking on his first-ever job managing an international team.

To help him get started, Xavi is bringing a familiar face with him. Former Dutch football legend Patrick Kluivert will be joining his coaching staff to work closely with him as an assistant.

Fans are very eager to see how Xavi will use his famous, fast-paced style of football to lead the Netherlands back to the top of the international stage.

articles.title: "We Came to Learn, Not to Sleep": Ghanaian Students Protest Massive Spike in Hostel Prices
articles.summary: Students across Ghana are heavily protesting the skyrocketing prices of private hostels. The movement is being led by organizations like NUGS and student groups from KNUST's Katanga Hall, and is now gaining official support, with the Unity Hall Master recently backing the students' demands for fair accommodation fees.

content.html:
University students across Ghana are standing up and demanding action. The cost of living around campus has become completely unaffordable.

Over the past few weeks, there has been a massive spike in the prices of private student hostels. The situation has gotten so bad that many students say they are now forced to pay much more for a simple bed than they actually pay for their university tuition.

This is not just an isolated problem. Almost every university in Ghana is facing the exact same issue.

At the University of Ghana, the prices are getting out of hand. For example, official rental rates for the 2026 academic year show that the cost for a single room at a major private alumni-built facility has jumped by massive, unmanageable amounts. Even a simple bed in a shared four-person room now costs a fortune.

Because of these crazy price hikes, the Acting Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, recently issued an official directive freezing any planned private hostel fee hikes for the 2026/2027 academic year until further notice. He even held a special meeting with the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Cape Coast (UCC), Prof. Denis Worlanyo Aheto, to discuss ways to enforce rent laws and protect students from these unfair, arbitrary charges.

To make matters worse, students at UCC are dealing with even more financial surprises. Student bodies have raised serious alarms about both school and accommodation fees being increased without any prior notice or proper consultation. Students often return for the new semester only to discover they owe much more money than they planned for, leaving them scrambling to find the extra funds at the last minute.

After receiving numerous complaints about these arbitrary price jumps, the UCC Students' Representative Council (SRC) President, Kwame Ntiamoah Ntim, officially directed all students to completely ignore and refuse to pay any unapproved hostel rent increases.

The anger recently boiled over at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). During the National Youth Conference held in Kumasi, members of the famous University Hall, widely known as Katanga, decided they had enough.

The Katanga morale group staged a peaceful but powerful protest right at the conference. They held up large signs with messages like 'Reduce hostel fees now!' and 'We came to learn, not to sleep'.

Obrane, a final-year Agricultural Engineering student and the leader of the morale group, spoke up for the crowd. He explained that these extreme prices are putting a terrible financial strain on parents who just want to see their children get a good education.

Student activist Selma Yoda recently went on national television to explain exactly how bad the living conditions are. She pointed out that at certain private complexes in Kumasi, rent has completely doubled, even though students still deal with water shortages, unpainted rooms, and broken facilities. The prices have become so severe that one female student was even forced to sleep in a church far from campus because she could not afford a room.

The National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) is also taking the fight directly to the authorities. NUGS President Rashid Ibrahim Esq. formally petitioned the Rent Control Department, pointing out that some private landlords are breaking the law by forcing students to pay for multiple years of rent in advance just to secure a room.

Their complaints are actually working. Following recent inspections, the Rent Control Commission and the Ghana Tourism Authority officially shut down two specific private facilities in Koforidua. They were closed because officials found poor sanitation and unacceptable living conditions, proving students were paying high prices for terrible rooms.

The Rent Control Department also recently began conducting surprise inspections at private hostels around the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) after students there complained about extreme, exploitative fees.

Housing advocates, like the National Tenants Union of Ghana, are warning the government that this is a full-blown housing crisis. They argue that the outdated Rent Act of 1963 needs to be overhauled because the institutions meant to protect citizens simply lack the resources to enforce the law.

The government is starting to step in to find a nationwide solution. George Opare Addo, the Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment, was at the KNUST conference and saw the protest. He publicly promised to take the issue straight to the Ministry of Education and the Rent Control Department.

He also shared some good news for the future. The government is currently talking to private developers to build more affordable housing directly on university campuses as part of a new 'Bed for All' agenda.

As the new school year gets closer, students all over the country are hoping these protests and official crackdowns will finally force landlords to bring their prices back down to a reasonable level.
