Student bodies have raised serious alarms about both school and accommodation fees being increased without any prior notice or proper consultation. Students often return for the new semester only to discover they owe much more money than they planned for, leaving them scrambling to find the extra funds at the last minute.

After receiving numerous complaints about these arbitrary price jumps, the UCC Students' Representative Council (SRC) President, Kwame Ntiamoah Ntim, officially directed all students to completely ignore and refuse to pay any unapproved hostel rent increases.

The anger recently boiled over at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). During the National Youth Conference held in Kumasi, members of the famous University Hall, widely known as Katanga, decided they had enough.
The Katanga morale group staged a peaceful but powerful protest right at the conference. They held up large signs with messages like 'Reduce hostel fees now!' and 'We came to learn, not to sleep'.

Obrane, a final-year Agricultural Engineering student and the leader of the morale group, spoke up for the crowd. He explained that these extreme prices are putting a terrible financial strain on parents who just want to see their children get a good education.

Student activist Selma Yoda recently went on national television to explain exactly how bad the living conditions are. She pointed out that at certain private complexes in Kumasi, rent has completely doubled, even though students still deal with water shortages, unpainted rooms, and broken facilities. The prices have become so severe that one female student was even forced to sleep in a church far from campus because she could not afford a room.

The National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) is also taking the fight directly to the authorities. NUGS President Rashid Ibrahim Esq. formally petitioned the Rent Control Department, pointing out that some private landlords are breaking the law by forcing students to pay for multiple years of rent in advance just to secure a room.

Their complaints are actually working. Following recent inspections, the Rent Control Commission and the Ghana Tourism Authority officially shut down two specific private facilities in Koforidua. They were closed because officials found poor sanitation and unacceptable living conditions, proving students were paying high prices for terrible rooms.

The Rent Control Department also recently began conducting surprise inspections at private hostels around the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) after students there complained about extreme, exploitative fees.

Housing advocates, like the National Tenants Union of Ghana, are warning the government that this is a full-blown housing crisis. They argue that the outdated Rent Act of 1963 needs to be overhauled because the institutions meant to protect citizens simply lack the resources to enforce the law.

The government is starting to step in to find a nationwide solution. George Opare Addo, the Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment, was at the KNUST conference and saw the protest. He publicly promised to take the issue straight to the Ministry of Education and the Rent Control Department.

He also shared some good news for the future. The government is currently talking to private developers to build more affordable housing directly on university campuses as part of a new 'Bed for All' agenda.
As the new school year gets closer, students all over the country are hoping these protests and official crackdowns will finally force landlords to bring their prices back down to a reasonable level.

articles.title: Tragic News: Ghanaian Evacuee Passes Away Upon Arrival in Accra
articles.summary: : A Ghanaian who was evacuated from South Africa sadly passed away shortly after arriving at the Kotoka International Airport in Accra on Friday evening

content.html:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has shared some very heartbreaking news. A Ghanaian citizen who was being evacuated from South Africa has tragically died right after arriving in Accra.

This sad event happened on the evening of Friday, August 14, 2026. The passenger was part of a group of 50 Ghanaians flying back home on an Air Tanzania flight. They were returning to Ghana to escape the recent attacks on foreigners in South Africa.

According to the official statement from the Ministry, other passengers noticed something was wrong during the trip. They reported that the person started feeling very sick about 30 minutes before the airplane even landed.

The flight officially touched down at the Kotoka International Airport at 5:50 p.m. A medical emergency team was already on standby at the airport waiting to receive the passengers. They immediately rushed to help the sick person and tried everything they could to save his life.

Sadly, their rescue attempts were not successful. Doctors confirmed that the passenger passed away at the airport's Emergency Medical Reception at exactly 6:55 p.m.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has stated that they are currently handling the formal process of contacting the family of the deceased. In the meantime, the person's body has been safely moved to the Police Hospital so medical experts can perform an autopsy to find out exactly why he died.

The Ghanaian government has been working very hard to bring over 1,600 citizens back home safely from South Africa, completely paying for the flights to protect them. While the rescue missions have been largely successful, this sudden loss is a very sad moment for the nation.
